strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear exposition of PIT limitations and auto-calibration necessity
Elegant theoretical framework: calibration-sharpness decomposition via generalized conditional mutual information (Lemma 4.1)
Principled nonparametric approach avoiding restrictive parametric assumptions of prior work
Energy Distance Kernel providing practical O(n log n) efficiency for real-valued targets
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, models (DRF, MDN, BNN, GDN), and metrics (SKCE, PIT, CRPS)
Clear presentation with good pedagogical motivation of calibration concepts
weaknesses: No convergence rates or sample complexity bounds for the CKME-based recalibration algorithm despite being core contribution
Distributional pre-image problem solved via ad-hoc Euclidean projection (Eq. 40) instead of principled approach, introducing unanalyzed approximation bias
Mixed empirical results: CRPS scores frequently deteriorate (Table 1), with PIT recalibration often remaining competitive or superior despite being deemed 'weak' calibration
Baseline None(T+C) often achieves comparable scores, suggesting simply using more training data may be preferable to post-hoc recalibration
Unfair GPBETA comparison due to inherent Gaussian approximation requirement; missing comparisons to temperature scaling and other simple post-hoc methods
Compactness assumption on target space Y (Remark 5.3) is non-trivial but only briefly discussed, limiting applicability
No real-world validation on high-stakes applications despite motivation; evaluation limited to UCI benchmarks where practical value of calibration improvements is unclear
Incremental novelty: combines existing techniques (CKME, SKCE, energy distance) with concurrent related work (Moskvichev & Sejdinovic 2025) targeting similar problem
O(n³) complexity for solving linear system (Eq. 10) remains prohibitive for large calibration sets despite O(n log n) kernel evaluation
Code availability URL missing; hyperparameter sensitivity (λ, bandwidth selection) not ablated; no analysis of failure modes

strengths: Well-motivated problem distinguishing weak PIT calibration from strong auto-calibration, with compelling examples
Solid technical contributions including the calibration-sharpness decomposition via generalized mutual information and the Energy Distance Kernel achieving O(n log n) efficiency
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, base models, and metrics (SKCE, PIT KS, CRPS) with detailed ablations
Clear presentation overall with complete algorithms and promised code availability
weaknesses: Mixed experimental results undermine practical significance: CKME frequently matches or underperforms None(T+C) in CRPS (Table 1), and PIT recalibration remains more effective (Figure 3). Many improvements are marginal.

Critical gap between theory and practice: the distributional pre-image approximation uses Euclidean projection (Eq. 40) instead of the principled optimization (Eq. 39), directly undermining Proposition 5.2's guarantees of auto-calibration and sharpness preservation. No analysis of how guarantees degrade in practice.

Motivation claims unsupported by evidence: paper emphasizes 'safety-critical applications' but provides no experiments on safety-critical datasets. UCI benchmarks with test sets ≤31 samples are unrepresentative and underpowered for hypothesis testing.

Finite sample behavior unanalyzed: no convergence rates, sample complexity bounds, or characterization of when theoretical guarantees hold empirically. Regularization λ selected via cross-validation on calibration set risks overfitting.
Restrictive assumptions limit applicability: requires Y to be compact metric space; assumes Q ⊥⊥ Y | X without discussing violations (e.g., model misspecification).

Computational complexity concerns: while EDK improves kernel matrix construction to O(nm log m + n²m), solving Eq. (10) costs O(n³_cal), dominating overall complexity. Wall-clock times (Figure 7) not dramatically faster than PIT.
Loss of density representation: method outputs empirical distributions, discarding continuous density of base models. Consequences for downstream tasks unexplored.
Incomplete experimental details: bandwidth σ selection ('median heuristic' not detailed), kernel l choice (Laplacian) unjustified, no hyperparameter sensitivity analysis.

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations of PIT-based calibration with clear practical relevance for safety-critical applications
Solid theoretical foundation including Lemma 4.1's elegant calibration-sharpness decomposition and proper grounding in generalized scoring rules and conditional mutual information
Novel nonparametric approach that meaningfully improves upon Song et al. (2019) by removing restrictive parametric assumptions while maintaining auto-calibration guarantees
Efficient Energy Distance Kernel achieving O(n log n) complexity for real-valued targets, providing practical algorithmic contribution
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 base models, 11 datasets, with multiple metrics (SKCE, PIT, CRPS) and extensive ablations in appendices
Clear presentation with effective motivation (autonomous vehicle example) and well-organized technical content
weaknesses: Marginal and inconsistent improvements in overall predictive accuracy (CRPS) across Table 1—CKME achieves better CRPS than None(T) in only ~50% of configurations, with None(T+C) frequently comparable, raising questions about practical value of calibration improvement without accuracy gains
Incomplete auto-calibration achievement—Figure 1 shows SKCE test acceptance only at 50-80% on many datasets, suggesting the method doesn't fully resolve the calibration problem it targets

Distributional pre-image problem solved via Euclidean projection (Eq. 40) as approximation to optimal solution (Eq. 39) without theoretical error bounds or empirical impact analysis, undermining principled nonparametric claims
Missing critical algorithmic sensitivity analyses: no ablations on regularization parameter λ, calibration set size requirements, kernel choice variations, or bandwidth selection robustness
Scalability concerns: despite EDK optimization, O(n³) complexity from linear system solving persists; Figure 7 shows CKME is actually slower than PIT recalibration in practice
Limited experimental scope: all datasets are small (<4500 samples), no high-dimensional targets tested, and evaluation on only real-valued regression setting

Insufficient justification for the calibration-without-accuracy trade-off—paper acknowledges satisfying calibration without sharpness is trivial but doesn't adequately resolve the inherent tension or demonstrate when practitioners should prioritize auto-calibration over predictive accuracy
